title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is a complex manifold, or the analytic space of a smooth complex variety. i: Y -> X is a closed submanifold of codimension p. The page checks that two Gysin (purity) maps are compatible with the comparison isomorphism C_X -> Omega^._X given by the holomorphic Poincaré lemma. The aim is that the topological and the analytic (Hodge/de Rham) fundamental classes of analytic cycles agree, up to an explicit normalising constant.

First diagram, three rows:
- Top row: the comparison isomorphism H^*(X,C) ~ H^*(X,Omega^._X).
- Middle row: the same comparison for cohomology with supports in Y, written as hypercohomology H^*(Y, i^!(-)), i.e. H^*_Y(X,-).
- Bottom row: H^*(Y,C) ~ H^*(Y,Omega^._Y).
- Upward maps from the middle row to the top row: forgetting supports. That square is labelled 'comm. (trivial)'.
- Upward maps from the bottom row to the middle row: the purity/Thom isomorphisms. P_top: H^{*-2p}(Y,C) -> H^*_Y(X,C) uses the topological Thom class. P_an: H^{*-2p}(Y,Omega^._Y) -> H^*_Y(X,Omega^._X) uses the analytic local fundamental class in H^p_Y(Omega^p_X) (Grothendieck residue / trace).
- For the lower square to commute, the bottom comparison map must be rescaled by (1/2iπ)^p.

Sheaf-level origin: this is said to come from a commutation at the level of sheaves. Namely C_Y[-2p] = i^!C -> i^!Omega^._X, compared with Omega^._Y via (1/2iπ)^p can. That commutation is in turn 'contained in the fundamental formulary' (the local computations of the fundamental class).

N.B.: analytic direct image (Gysin in Hodge/de Rham cohomology) does not send integral classes to integral classes. One needs the factor 1/(2iπ)^p.

Boxed conclusion: for analytic cycles of codimension i, the square commutes.
- One side: A^i(X) -> H^{2i}(X,Z) (topological cycle class), then H^{2i}(X,Z) -> H^{2i}(X,C).
- Other side: A^i(X) -> H^{2i}(X,Omega^._X) via (1/2iπ)^i P_an, then the comparison isomorphism to H^{2i}(X,C).

This is the standard compatibility of the Betti and de Rham cycle class maps up to (2πi)^codim. It is the bookkeeping that underlies the definition of the Hodge realization and of the Tate twist Z(1) = 2πi Z, here in the context of motives and Hodge theory.
errors: In the first diagram the bottom horizontal arrow is labelled 1/(2iπ) can; consistency with the sheaf-level diagram requires (1/2iπ)^p.
In the boxed diagram the exponent is written p, but the cycles have codimension i; it should be (1/2iπ)^i.

Degree shifts by 2p in the purity maps P_top and P_an are suppressed. The direction and convention of the factor (multiply or divide by (2πi)^p) depends on how the analytic fundamental class / residue is normalised; this is not specified.

ideas.what: Compatibility of topological and analytic (Hodge / de Rham) Gysin and cycle class maps via local cohomology i^! and the holomorphic Poincaré lemma, with normalising factor (2πi)^{-p}
ideas.modern_name: Comparison of Betti and de Rham cycle classes; Tate twist Z(p) = (2πi)^p Z in the Betti-de Rham comparison
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties, 1966; letters), Hartshorne (Residues and Duality / de Rham cohomology), Deligne (Théorie de Hodge II, 1971), El Zein (Classe fondamentale d'un cycle, 1978)
ideas.where_published: Factor (2πi) discussed in Grothendieck's 1966 IHES paper on algebraic de Rham cohomology; the fully worked version is in Deligne's Hodge II and El Zein

ideas.what: Integral analytic Gysin image requires dividing by (2iπ)^p
ideas.modern_name: Integral structure of the de Rham cycle class; period normalisation

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard verification that the Betti and de Rham cycle classes match up to (2πi)^codim. It is well documented in Deligne's and El Zein's work and is part of the standard setup of Hodge realizations of motives.
transcription_corrections: The bottom-left entry of the first diagram looks like H^*_{(struck)}(Y,C), with a struck-out subscript; it is effectively H^*(Y,C).
The phrase after the second diagram reads plausibly 'lui-même contenu dans le formulaire fondamental'.
The exponent in the boxed diagram is written p by Grothendieck, though i is meant.
